item: [L2] Frozen fixtures: a text-based PDF (CJK font embedded) ... (fixture.pdf)
why: The PDF must embed a real Traditional Chinese font so its pages look like a normal spec document to every kind of converter (text-layer, layout-model or OCR based). No such font may be written by hand or copied in without a licence decision. make_pdf.py embeds only a subset (about 150 glyphs) and keeps the font's name table, which carries its copyright and licence notice; the font file itself is not committed. It needs TrueType outlines (a glyf table), static Regular and Bold files preferred.

candidates.source: https://github.com/google/fonts/tree/main/ofl/notosanstc (also offered as a family download on https://fonts.google.com/noto/specimen/Noto+Sans+TC)
candidates.license: SIL Open Font License 1.1 (embedding in documents allowed)
candidates.size: not downloaded; CJK TrueType files are typically several MB to tens of MB, record the real size
candidates.pin: Use the static NotoSansTC-Regular.ttf and NotoSansTC-Bold.ttf if the download contains them. The repository file is a variable font, whose default instance may be a very light weight: make_pdf.py warns and prints the weight class. Record the google/fonts commit or download date and the sha256 of each .ttf in calibration.md.

candidates.source: https://github.com/ButTaiwan/genyog-font (GenYoGothic TW, a Traditional Chinese sans serif)
candidates.size: not downloaded; record the real size
candidates.pin: Pick a release tag; confirm after download that the Regular and Bold files have glyf outlines (make_pdf.py refuses CFF). Record tag and sha256 of each file.

candidates.size: not downloaded; record the real size
candidates.pin: Single weight: run make_pdf.py without --bold-font (headings then use fill+stroke bold). Record release tag and sha256.

item: [L2] Egress check passes during the conversions; With egress blocked ... (all q05 L2 checks)
why: The check scripts need python3 and the egress check needs strace; ubuntu:24.04 ships neither. Both are grader tools, not part of any answer. Installing them changes the image the answers run in, so the choice must be the same for both groups and recorded.

candidates.source: Ubuntu 24.04 (noble) archive: apt-get install -y python3 strace
candidates.size: a few tens of MB installed
candidates.pin: Bake them into the grading image (dev image + python3 + strace) before any answer runs; record `dpkg-query -W python3 strace` and the image digest in calibration.md. Alternative: install them only after the answer's install steps finished (then L2-1 runs on the untouched dev image); pick one and use it for both groups.

item: [L2] The install steps succeed verbatim in the dev image (x86_64, CPU only, 4 vCPU and 16 GB)
why: The dev image is the same image family as the product's sandbox verification (eval/README.md section 5); its exact digest has to be fixed and recorded before the first run so both groups use the same one.

candidates.source: The Modal Sandbox image built on ubuntu:24.04 that the product's sandbox verification uses
candidates.pin: Record the image digest, Modal sandbox settings (cpu=4, memory=16384 MiB, no GPU) and region in calibration.md.
